questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The speech you made today was __sillier__ and irrelevant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**silly**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The original sentence uses "sillier and irrelevant." The word "irrelevant" is in its positive (base) form.
 
• When two adjectives are joined by "and" and describe the same noun, they should generally be in the same degree of comparison.
 
• Since "irrelevant" is a positive adjective (not comparative or superlative), "sillier" (which is a comparative adjective) creates an imbalance.
 
• Therefore, "**silly**" (मूर्खतापूर्ण) is the correct positive degree adjective to match "irrelevant," making the sentence grammatically parallel and correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

Complete Sentence: *"The speech you made today was silly__ and irrelevant."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1: "silliest"** – This is the superlative form, used for comparing three or more things. It would not match "irrelevant."
 
• **Option 3: "most silly"** – This is an alternative superlative form, also not matching "irrelevant."
 
• **Option 4: "more silly"** – This is an alternative comparative form, but it would still be a comparative, mismatching "irrelevant."

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

She showed this plant and talked about __it's medicinal properties__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. its medicinal properties .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined segment in the sentence is **"it's medicinal properties".**
 
• The word **"it's"** is a contraction of **"it is"** or **"it has"**, which is incorrect in this context.
 
• Here, the possessive form **"its"** (without an apostrophe) should be used to indicate that the medicinal properties belong to the plant.
 
• Thus, the correct substitution for the underlined part is **"its medicinal properties".**

Correct sentence: *She showed this plant and talked about **its medicinal properties**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Confusion:**

 
 
• **It's:** Contraction of *"it is"* or *"it has"*.
 
• **Its:** Possessive form of *"it"*, used to indicate ownership.
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• **Incorrect:** The dog wagged it's tail.
 
• **Correct:** The dog wagged its tail.

questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select "No error".

She learnt / how to play a piano / when she was in Class 6th.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. how to play a piano .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains an error in the phrase **"how to play a piano."**
 
• The article **"a"** is incorrect here because the word **"piano"** is typically used with the definite article **"the"** when referring to playing the instrument.
 
• The correct usage is **"how to play the piano."**

Correct sentence: *She learnt how to play the piano when she was in Class 6th.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Articles:**

 
 
• **"The"** is used before instruments when talking about playing them, e.g., *"play the guitar," "play the piano."*
 
• **"A" or "An"** is used when referring to one among many or something non-specific, e.g., *"I bought a piano."*
 
 
 
• **Example Sentences:**
 
 
• She knows how to play the violin.
 
• He is learning how to play the drums.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'isolated' from the given sentence.

A Greek mythological story says that Echo was the most beautiful nymph who lived in the lovely and lonely mountains of Greece and is believed to be garrulous too.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 (Lonely)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"isolated"** means being separated from others, far away from people or other things. It refers to a state of being alone or detached. (अलग-थलग)

 
 
• **Example:** The small island is completely isolated from the mainland.
 
 
 
• **"Lonely"** refers to being without company or feeling alone, which is a synonym of "isolated." (अकेला)
 
 
• **Example:** After moving to a new city, she often felt lonely without her friends and family.
 
 
 
• Hence, the most appropriate synonym for "isolated" in the given sentence is **"lonely."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 (Lonely)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Garrulous** (बातूनी): Excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters.

 
 
• **Example:** The garrulous old man entertained the children with his endless stories.
 
 
 
• **Beautiful** (सुंदर): Pleasing to the senses or mind aesthetically.
 
 
• **Example:** The sunset over the hills was truly beautiful.
 
 
 
• **Lovely** (आकर्षक): Exquisitely beautiful or charming.
 
 
• **Example:** She wore a lovely dress to the wedding.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The act of transferring one's authority to another
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Delegation**.

__
 
• The word **"Delegation"** refers to the act of transferring one's authority or responsibility to another person or group. (प्रतिनिधित्व या अधिकार सौंपना)

 
 
• **Example:** The manager made a delegation of tasks to the team leaders to ensure timely project completion.
 
 
 
• **"Authority transfer"** involves assigning responsibilities or powers from one person to another, often seen in workplaces or organizational structures. (अधिकार हस्तांतरण)

• **Example:** The mediary helped resolve the dispute between the two companies.
 
 
 
• **Agency** (संस्था ): An organization or business that provides a particular service or represents another.
 
 
• **Example:** The travel agency arranged our entire trip to Europe.
 
 
 
• **Assignee** (प्रत्यायित व्यक्ति): A person to whom rights, responsibilities, or properties are transferred.
 
 
• **Example:** The assignee will handle the estate after the owner's demise.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

"It's really ________ to incorporate changes at the last minute," she said.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**difficult**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• The word "**difficult**" is an adjective and fits appropriately in the blank to describe the situation.

• The sentence refers to the challenges of incorporating changes at the last minute, so the adjective "**difficult**" is required.

• **Options 1** and **2** ("difficulty" and "difficulties") are incorrect because they are nouns and do not match the required adjective form.

• **Option 4** ("most difficult") is incorrect because it implies a comparison, which is not present in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"It's really **difficult**__ to incorporate changes at the last minute," she said.*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Option 1: "difficulty"** is incorrect because it is a noun, and the sentence requires an adjective.

• **Option 2: "difficulties"** is incorrect for the same reason as Option 1—it is a plural noun.

• **Option 4: "most difficult"** is incorrect because no comparison is being made in the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Despite the setbacks, the team decided to persevere and keep working on the project, believing it could be a _______ for their company.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**game-changer**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**game-changer**" refers to a new and innovative event, idea, or development that significantly impacts the current situation or changes the course of events.
 
• In the given context, the team believed their project could be a "game-changer" for their company, implying it had the potential to bring about a significant positive shift.
 
• The other options: "**beat around the bush**" (avoid the main topic), "**needle in a haystack**" (something extremely hard to find), and "**wild goose chase**" (a futile or hopeless pursuit) do not fit the context appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Despite the setbacks, the team decided to persevere and keep working on the project, believing it could be a game-changer__ for their company.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Beat around the bush:** To avoid discussing the main topic or issue.
 
• **Needle in a haystack:** Something that is extremely difficult or impossible to find.
 
• **Wild goose chase:** A pointless or hopeless pursuit.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

The judge declared that the red car went _______ than the blue car.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**farther**'. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 

• The adjective "**farther**" is used to compare distances between two objects or actions. 

• In this sentence, the comparison is made between the distances traveled by the red car and the blue car. 

• **Option 1:** "more far" is grammatically incorrect as "farther" is the correct comparative form of "far." 

• **Option 3:** "far" is incorrect as it does not compare the two distances. 

• **Option 4:** "farthest" is incorrect because it indicates the superlative degree, which is used to compare more than two objects. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The judge declared that the red car went **farther**__ than the blue car."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
 

• **Option 1:** "more far" is not standard English usage. Always use "farther" for comparative distance. 

• **Option 3:** "far" does not provide a comparative sense, which is required in this context. 

• **Option 4:** "farthest" is used when comparing more than two objects or actions, which is not the case here.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

It is worth noting that the __possible from him__ being voted as the class monitor is next to zero.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. possibility of him .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"possible from him"** is incorrect because it does not convey the intended meaning in the sentence.
 
• The correct phrase to use is **"possibility of him"**, as it aligns grammatically and contextually with the sentence.
 
• The word **"possibility"** is a noun, and it is correctly followed by the preposition **"of"** to introduce the person or thing involved.

Correct sentence: *It is worth noting that the **possibility of him** being voted as the class monitor is next to zero*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Errors:**

 
 
• Using **"possible of"** instead of **"possibility of"** is incorrect, as "possible" is an adjective and cannot serve as a noun in this context.
 
• Using **"possibility at"** or **"possibly of"** is grammatically incorrect and does not fit the sentence structure.
 
 
 
• **Usage of "possibility of":**
 
 
• **Example:** The possibility of rain tomorrow is high.
 
• **Explanation:** "Possibility" refers to the chance of something happening, and "of" connects it to the subject or event.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. One of them contains an error. Select the segment that contains the error from the given options.

She has been speaking to him on the subject many times.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. She has been speaking .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence lies in the usage of **"has been speaking"**.
 
• The phrase **"has been speaking"** is incorrect in this context because the action described (speaking many times) is not continuous or ongoing. It should be expressed using the **simple present perfect tense**, i.e., "has spoken."
 
• The correct form of the sentence should be **"She has spoken to him on the subject many times."**

Correct sentence: *She has spoken to him on the subject many times.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Continuous:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + has/have been + verb-ing.
 
• **Example:** She has been working on the project since morning.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to actions that started in the past and are still ongoing.
 
 
 
• **Present Perfect:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + has/have + past participle.
 
• **Example:** He has finished his homework.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to actions completed in the past but with relevance to the present.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
